verdict.rationale: Sill pairs each iPhone or iPad with the Mac once. After that, only paired devices can connect, and Launch at Login keeps the host running without anyone opening it, so pre-paired access is implied. Remote Access via VPN or port forwarding extends this beyond the local network. Initial pairing still needs a code scan, a USB cable, or a tap while the Mac is unlocked. missing for 10: an explicit statement that later connections need no acceptance at the host, access when the Mac is locked or at the login window, admin-provisioned credentials or mass deployment without touching each host, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can set up unattended access to a machine with credentials configured in advance, so no one has to sit at the host to accept

citations.quote: Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
To have Sill open by itself then, choose Launch at Login in the Sill menu, or turn it on in Sill’s Settings › General.
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
